classification.difficultyReason: Use the preliminary length and angle results to select opposite pairs in triangle ABD, substitute them into the sine rule, and simplify a supplementary-angle sine to prove the symbolic expression.

inlines.text: [Preliminary step to prove the sine compound-angle formula]

spec.description: A, B and C are collinear in that order. D is vertically above C. AD and BD are drawn; AB is labelled x, AC has a separate double-ended dimension arrow labelled y, and CD is labelled h. Angles beta at A and alpha between BC and BD are marked, with a right angle at C.
spec.mathematics: AB=x, AC=y, CD=h, angle DAC=beta, angle DBC=alpha, angle BCD=90 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied givens and angle marks are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Write an expression for the length of $AD$ in terms of $h$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Express $\angle BDA$ and $\angle ABD$ in terms of the unknown angles in the triangles.

answer.worked:
Since $A$, $B$ and $C$ lie on a straight line,
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABD&=180^\circ-\alpha.\end{align*}$$
Using the angle sum of triangle $ABD$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle BDA&=180^\circ-\beta-(180^\circ-\alpha)\\\angle BDA&=\alpha-\beta.\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$h=\dfrac{x\sin\beta\sin\alpha}{\sin(\alpha-\beta)}$.

Apply the sine rule in $ABD$, using the results from parts (a) and (b).
answer.worked:
Apply the sine rule in triangle $ABD$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AD}{\sin\angle ABD}&=\frac{AB}{\sin\angle BDA}\\\frac{h}{\sin\beta\sin(180^\circ-\alpha)}&=\frac{x}{\sin(\alpha-\beta)}.\end{align*}$$
Since $\sin(180^\circ-\alpha)=\sin\alpha$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{h}{\sin\beta\sin\alpha}&=\frac{x}{\sin(\alpha-\beta)}\\h&=\frac{x\sin\beta\sin\alpha}{\sin(\alpha-\beta)}.\end{align*}$$
